The market board operates under exchange consensus, where book lines are authoritative and synthetic lines are strictly prohibited. In contrast, the signal board embodies model-driven inference, where synthetic lines are inherently absent and labels are derived from predictive models. This separation ensures that GSI's Bayesian inference remains grounded in empirical signal rather than speculative consensus. The freshness criteria—odds insertion and seed pick publication—act as dual thresholds ensuring temporal validity. The LIVE_BOARD maintains consistency across both surfaces, enforcing a robust state transition mechanism in GSE. Failure modes arise when synthetic lines masquerade as book lines or when freshness thresholds are violated, leading to integrity loss.
